stages.title: The terminal baseline
stages.summary: One C process handles keyboard input, ASCII rendering, the elevator state machine and runtime guardrails. Requests share a single set of floor buttons.

stages.title: A web interface, a C runtime
stages.summary: The browser adds animated floors, cabin controls and passenger journeys. A C HTTP server and passenger dispatcher handle shared trips, capacity and intermediate stops.

stages.title: A door to the internet
stages.summary: An outbound Cloudflare tunnel exposes the C service through public HTTPS. The backend accepts the exact configured public hostname and Origin, with C running on port 8099.

stages.title: Experiments that stay with you
stages.summary: Embedded SQLite retains 10 Hz elevator samples, events, passenger timings and textual feedback. Named runs, historical queries and JSON/CSV exports support experimentation.

stages.title: Direct network access
stages.summary: Explicit IPv4 binding and hostname aliases allow direct access on port 8099 alongside the HTTPS tunnel. Host, port and Origin checks remain in the C server.

stages.title: The system tells its story
stages.summary: An evolution timeline brings every stage's architecture and sequence diagrams into the web interface. A shared catalog, generated assets and freshness checks keep future steps traceable.

stages.title: Watch the current run unfold
stages.summary: Dashboard shortcuts expose the diagram history, a live sequence follows the current simulation run, and combined JSON/CSV exports include every recorded data kind.

stages.title: The Metriczone measurement lab
stages.summary: The supplied Metriczone logo shapes a deep teal and white interface, geometric typography and measurement-focused dashboard. Controls, live diagrams and experimentation tools share the new identity.

stages.title: Readable code, traceable behavior
stages.summary: Comments follow the guardrail module's conventions across the authored C backend, web interface, tools and tests. Module purpose, function contracts and inline explanations document the existing behavior.

stages.title: Traffic you can repeat, steering you can improve
stages.summary: Runnable morning, afternoon, occasional, VIP and custom traffic scenarios use a C arrival scheduler. Selected-run telemetry analysis explains measured bottlenecks and suggests steering experiments.

stages.title: Elevator-first interface and autoevolution workflow
stages.summary: The elevator and controls precede scenarios and telemetry. Direct wording explains simulation, steering analysis and the autoevolution workflow; diagnostics and stage history remain available.

stages.title: Source modules and dependencies
stages.summary: Architecture diagrams show stage-specific C files, public headers, web components and tooling dependencies. Current C, web and deployment modules have separate views; sequences retain runtime behavior.

stages.title: Restart-safe POSIX HTTP listener
stages.summary: The C server enables POSIX address reuse before binding, reports OS socket errors and retains active-listener exclusion. Telemetry HTTP tests verify three immediate restarts on the same port and database.
